episodes.170111: A brief period of heavy rainfall caused mud and rocks to cover Highway 125, as anywhere from 0.25 to 0.50 inches of rain fell in 30 minutes.  The highway was closed between Trail Creek and Coral Cabin Creek Road (FR 112).  There was some road damage with a large area of mud and rocks covering the roadway.  Two bulldozers were brought out to remove the debris.
episodes.170123: Severe thunderstorms that developed early Saturday morning across northern South Dakota, moved eastward over west-central Minnesota. Several clusters of storms developed as the main system continued to propagate to the east-southeast during the morning across southern Minnesota. Most of the storms were pulse type and only produced isolated large hail or severe wind gusts. However, a couple of the storms managed to organize across Renville and Sibley Counties of southern Minnesota, and produced up to 3 inch diameter hail near Gibbon. In addition to the hail, severe wind gusts of 70 mph were reported at the Olivia airport, along with several large trees blown down. Another cluster of storms managed to organize near Mankato, to Kenyon by the late morning. The worst damage occurred in Kenyon where uprooted trees caused power outages in the town. Severe storms developed later in the evening and produced a 66 mph wind gust at the Waseca airport, and destroyed a barn northeast of Bixby in Steele County.
episodes.170124: Thunderstorms developed in a strongly unstable environment with weak flow. A few of these storms reached severe limits.
episodes.170126: In the Glen Haven and Crystal Mountain areas heavy rain produced flash flooding.  Radar estimated 0.50 to 0.75 inch of rain in 30 minutes.  Miller Fork washed over Larimer County Road 43 at Streamside Drive near The Retreat, closing the roadway.  Streamside Drive was damaged but passable.  Black Creek Drive in The Retreat was damaged pretty significantly.  Every stream crossing along Black Creek Drive was reportedly washed out.  There was a 6-foot drop at the first stream crossing on that road. Buckhorn Creek washed over Wildsong Road, and Sheep Creek washed across LCR 44H with minor damage reported.   Deer Path and Wildsong became impassable by vehicle.||In Morgan County, heavy rain from 1.5 to 3.5 inches produced flash flooding.  A couple of county roads around Brush were flooded.  One of those roads was completely washed out.  The basement of a residence was also flooded.
episodes.170128: It was a typical monsoon day across northern and central New Mexico on July 23, 2022, as an abundant amount of moisture led to scattered to numerous thunderstorms. The Hermits Peak and Calf Canyon burn scar proved once again to be the area of most concern as heavy rainfall on the northern end of the burn area led to flash flooding. The Holman and Cleveland areas, which have been hardest hit so far this summer, were hit hard again with flash flooding and debris flow.
episodes.170167: Multiple lines of strong to severe storms developed over southern Wisconsin on the evening of July 23rd through the morning hours of July 24th. The first round of storms was particularly strong and brought high winds to the Lake Michigan shoreline.
episodes.170187: Several rounds of early evening thunderstorms on the 24th caused isolated pockets of tree damage across central Indiana with sub-severe hail also across Hendricks county.  By late into the evening, a series of storms moved across Knox county with areas of rainfall over 6 inches.  Significant flash flooding occurred across the county with a road washed out and water rescues conducted.
episodes.170485: An upper-level trough moved into the Treasure State from the west. SPC placed several counties in a Marginal Risk for severe thunderstorms, including southern Judith Basin County, Meagher and Broadwater Counties, and northern Gallatin County with the remainder of the CWA under a general risk. Primary impact was heavy rain, but had possible lightning, small hail, and erratic winds associated with the storm.
episodes.170674: Evening sea breeze thunderstorms produce gusty winds over the coastal waters.
episodes.170695: Two rounds of convection impacted Pennsylvania on July 24, 2022. The first round of convection involved a cluster of storms that pushed across the northern mountains (along and north of I-80) during the afternoon hours, producing sporadic wind damage. The second round of convection was in the form of a line of thunderstorms just ahead of a cold front approaching northwestern Pennsylvania from the Great Lakes during the late evening of July 24 into the early morning hours of July 25. This second round of convection produced sporadic wind damage across northwestern Pennsylvania before weakening as it progressed southeastward overnight.
episodes.170867: A cold front sparked showers and thunderstorms, some of which resulted in gusty winds near Baltimore Inner Harbor and the tidal Potomac River.
episodes.170977: Several rounds of strong thunderstorms produced gusty winds as they tracked over the Lake Michigan waters during from the late afternoon on Saturday (7/23) through the early morning hours on Sunday (7/24).
episodes.171118: Storms developed in the warm sector of a system resulting in a couple of hail reports and widespread wind damage with peak winds nearly reaching 90 mph.
episodes.171119: Storms developed in the warm sector of a system resulting in widespread wind damage with peak winds nearly reaching 90 mph.
episodes.171210: Scattered thunderstorms moved across southern Lake Michigan during the morning of July 24th producing strong winds.
episodes.171305: The Upper Midwest was under the gun on July 23rd, with SPC forecasting damaging thunderstorm wind gusts (some of 75 mph), very large hail, and a few tornadoes. As convection was ongoing well to our northwest, diurnally driven showers and thunderstorms had popped up across eastern KY amid a warm and moist airmass in place. WPC analyzed an outflow boundary dropping south across the Ohio Valley from the larger area of main convection. By the time it made it into eastern KY, this likely served as a extra boundary to lead to destabalization and strengthening of a couple of the storms. Several localized thunderstorm wind reports were made before storms eventually fizzled out heading into the ovenright hours with loss of daytime forcing.||An area of storms northeast of the state during the morning hours eventually made their way southeast and into eastern Kentucky by the late afternoon and evening.
episodes.171325: Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and evening of the 24th across northern Aroostook county within the warm humid air in advance of an approaching cold front. A severe supercell thunderstorm developed across northwest Aroostook county during the late afternoon and tracked northeast across northern Aroostook county through the early evening. The thunderstorm produced damaging winds and large hail at various times along its path. The maximum hail size reported was around 2.50 inches...with wind gusts estimated at up to 90 mph at times. The storm tracked through wooded areas along much of its path.
episodes.171334: A thunderstorm over the adjacent coastal waters produced a waterspout.
episodes.171346: Mainly between 3:30-6:30 p.m. CDT on this Saturday afternoon, a relatively narrow, southwest-northeast swath of South Central Nebraska experienced severe thunderstorms featuring several reports of damaging winds up to around 70 MPH and hail up to ping pong ball size. The vast majority of local severe activity unfolded within 10 miles either side of a line extending from Elwood-Overton-Ravenna-St. Paul-Wolbach. Within this corridor, the most notable wind damage occurred within and very near Howard County, as places extending from just east of Farwell and through the St. Paul, Elba and Wolbach areas experienced winds estimated to at least 65-70 MPH, causing fairly extensive tree damage and also taking down some irrigation pivots and power lines. Outside of this main area of damaging wind (and earlier in the event), the highest unofficial mesonet-measured wind gust of 60 MPH occurred in Elm Creek. Also outside the main severe wind zone (and a bit later in the evening) a rogue, briefly severe storm that flared up behind the main activity blew down a large tree in a neighborhood along the Platte River near Central City. As for hail, the largest reported stones to ping pong ball size occurred between Lexington and Overton (including at the Overton golf course) and also in rural northwestern Buffalo County. ||Breaking down event evolution/timing, this was a fairly classic setup for high-based severe storms, largely driven by a combination of intense heating and decent low level convergence along a well-defined summer cold front gradually tracking across Nebraska from northwest-to-southeast. Storms first ignited just southwest of the local area (near McCook) shortly before 3 p.m. CDT in a very hot/deeply mixed airmass (shortly before initiation the McCook airport reported a temp/dewpoint of 107/56 F). Between 3:30-4:30 p.m. CDT strong to severe storms quickly unzipped northeastward along the frontal zone into western portions of South Central Nebraska, assuming a mix of multicell and brief supercell structures as they first impacted primarily Gosper/Dawson/Buffalo counties. Over the next few hours, the most intense storms marched across parts of mainly Sherman, Howard, eastern Greeley and far western Nance counties before departing the local area into eastern Nebraska by around 6:30 p.m. CDT. In the wake of this main event, mostly weak convection roamed predominantly southern/eastern portions of South Central Nebraska well into the night...with the briefly-severe storm near Central City around 8 p.m. CDT serving as the last gasp of anything feisty. Getting back to the meteorological setup, this event was fairly weakly-forced in the mid-upper levels, with southern Nebraska residing along the southern fringes of modestly-strong, quasi-zonal flow directed between an upper ridge centered over the Southern Rockies and a trough centered far to the north over southern Canada. As mentioned, the main player at the surface was the invading cold front, with the combination of frontal forcing and intense heating/stout instability proving sufficient to overcome notable capping (evidenced by 700 millibar temperatures averaging 14-16 C). This was actually one of the top-5 hottest days of 2022 across the majority of South Central Nebraska, with most stations topping out between 99-106 F.  Through most of this event, the local mesoscale environment featured 1000-3000 J/kg mixed-layer CAPE and 30-35 knots of deep layer wind shear.
episodes.171442: A shortwave trough was the main feature out of a few disturbances that triggered a line of thunderstorms that passed through Northeastern Pennsylvania. These storms had damaging wind gusts and knocked down numerous trees across the region. Some of the debris landed on houses and vehicles. One person was injured after they were hit by a falling tree.
episodes.171444: A shortwave trough was the main feature out of a few disturbances that triggered a line of thunderstorms that passed through Central New York. These storms had damaging wind gusts and knocked down numerous trees across the region. Some trees and debris landed on vehicles or structures. There were also a couple reports of fires started from downed wires.
episodes.171546: A severe thunderstorm impacted Shiawassee County producing wind damage.
episodes.171548: An isolated severe thunderstorm occurred across eastern Stillwater County and Southwest Yellowstone County during the early evening hours on the 24th. This thunderstorm produced large hail, very high wind gusts and torrential rain.
episodes.171573: A shortwave pushed across the Midwest, resulting a a period of severe storms. the leading moisture axis and warm front were confined main to Minnesota in the afternoon, though a few stronger storms skimmed northern Iowa with a hail report in Winnebago county. The cold front passed across Iowa later in the evening from western to northern Iowa. Modest CAPE was in place but with strong deep layer shear over 40 kts and drier low levels noted in model soundings, gusty winds were the primary hazard with this second round of thunderstorms. Winds gusted over 60 mph with a few reports of damage to trees and outbuildings.
episodes.171590: Several rounds of severe thunderstorms tracked along a warm front over southern WI from the afternoon of July 23rd into the early morning hours of July 24th. Numerous reports of wind damage were received. Destructive, large hail and flash flooding also occurred.
episodes.171821: Isolated thunderstorms developed along the sea breeze in a typical summertime atmosphere across portions of southeast South Carolina. One storm became severe and produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.171822: Isolated thunderstorms developed along the sea breeze in a typical summertime atmosphere across portions of southeast Georgia. As these storms progressed inland they produced outflow boundaries and gusty winds that caused some minor wind damage.
episodes.171824: Scattered thunderstorms developed along an outflow boundary near I-70 during the afternoon. As clusters of storms moved southeast during the evening, additional development behind the initial storms resulted in multiple rounds of thunderstorms over the same areas. More than 4 inches of rain fell in Lawrence County in six hours, producing isolated flash flooding. The storms also produced an isolated strong wind gust.
episodes.172024: As a cold front moved south through the region, showers and storms developed. A few of the storms produced damaging winds and large hail.
episodes.172049: Severe thunderstorms bringing wind gusts in the 60 to 72 mph range brought down several trees, tree limbs and power lines across portions of southern and south central lower Michigan.  One fatality occurred just north of downtown Grand Rapids when a large hinged steel door on a shipping container was blown onto a man.
episodes.172125: Severe thunderstorms developed within a hot and humid air mass across portions of eastern New York, especially for areas south of Interstate 90, during the afternoon and evening hours on July 24, 2022. Widespread wind damage occurred across these areas.||More than 20,000 customers lost power across Ulster and Dutchess counties including in Esopus, Rosendale, Kingston, Saugerties, Wawarsing, Hyde Park, Pleasant Valley and Poughkeepsie. Sporadic pockets of outages also occurred across the Capital Region and into portions of Rensselaer and Columbia counties.
episodes.172152: A few rounds of thunderstorms on July 24th and 25th preceded a cold frontal passage.  High levels of instability, ample shear, and pre-frontal disturbances provided thunderstorm clusters producing widespread damaging wind gusts.  Many instances of tree and power line damage were noted, along with isolated instances of structural damage.  One of those instances of structural damage, a tree falling on to two trailers in Venango County, unfortunately led to the death of a 28 year old woman.  Flash flooding of urbanized areas of Allegheny County also occurred.
episodes.172154: A few rounds of thunderstorms on July 24th and 25th preceded a cold frontal passage.  High levels of instability, ample shear, and pre-frontal disturbances provided thunderstorm clusters producing widespread damaging wind gusts, nearly all of which occurred further north, but one instance of wind damage was reported in Ohio County.
episodes.172207: A weather system crossed Wyoming on July 24th, encouraging thunderstorm development. Severe thunderstorm winds occurred in multiple locations across northern and central Wyoming. At the Lander airport, a maximum wind gust of 74 mph was recorded. In Park County, wind gusts of 60 to 70 mph were reported. In Cody, 400 customers lost power when trees were downed by the wind and fell on power lines.
episodes.172214: Two rounds of storms moved across southeast Minnesota on July 23rd. The first occurred in the afternoon and produced two tornadoes, wind damage and large hail. A brief EF0 tornado occurred south of Fremont (Winona County) that produced mainly tree damage. Another EF0 tornado touched down just north of Houston (Houston County) and damaged a barn and trees along its path. The storms also produced high winds that damaged structures in Claremont (Dodge County), blew down trees in numerous locations, and produced 66 mph gusts in downtown Rochester (Olmsted County) and near Brownsdale (Mower County) and Sheldon (Houston County). The largest reported hail was quarter sized near Oronoco (Olmsted County). The second round of storms occurred in the late evening, producing dime sized hail near Spring Valley (Fillmore County) before moving into northeast Iowa. Houston County declared a state of emergency following the storms.
episodes.172292: Isolated severe thunderstorms occurred across the far eastern plains during the evening hours, with damaging wind gusts up to 75 mph occurring across Prowers County.
episodes.172294: Isolated thunderstorms once again occurred across the eastern plains. Damage was not widespread, though some significant damage did occur across the northwest portion of Prowers County.
episodes.172333: A weak surface trough combined with high instability triggered scattered afternoon thunderstorms. A couple of these storms damaging winds and large hail.
episodes.172346: Several waves of convection moved through the region during the afternoon and first half of the ensuing night as a slow moving cold front approached from southern Ontario. The event was long lived due to high instability and strong shear. The first round of convection broke out along a lake breeze boundary that stretched from the Finger Lakes region back across the Southern Tier.  The next round of storms that developed after sunset produced wind damage and also very heavy rain. This was a rare event in that back to back severe thunderstorm watches were issued across the NWS Buffalo county warning area.
episodes.172347: Several waves of convection moved through the region during the afternoon and first half of the ensuing night as a slow moving cold front approached from southern Ontario. The event was long lived due to high instability and shear. The first round of convection broke out along a lake breeze boundary that stretched from the Finger Lakes region back across the Southern Tier. episodes.172351: A weakening MCS moved into central Virginia during the evening on July 23, providing enough lift for a brief severe thunderstorm.
episodes.172428: Under the influence of the North Atlantic subtropical high, classic summer time storms developed within an environment conducive to microbursts. Isolated reports of wind damage occurred within close proximity to the strongest downdrafts, especially across the central Piedmont.
episodes.172429: A surface Piedmont trough over western North Carolina led to the development of isolated to scattered thunderstorms in the afternoon and early evening across the Piedmont of central North Carolina. Some of these storms produced wind damage over Harnett and Moore Counties. Another round of isolated thunderstorms moved into the northwest Piedmont associated with a mid-level disturbance in the late evening to early overnight hours, producing a single severe wind event in the Triad.
episodes.172445: A moisture-rich environment was in place on the 24th with PWAT values climbing upwards of 2 across south-central Arizona. A weak disturbance embedded in the flow aided in shower and thunderstorm development to persist out of southeast Arizona and into central portions of the state. Given the amount of moisture in the environment, thunderstorms were able to produce locally heavy rainfall which led to isolated flash flooding in southern Maricopa County. By the afternoon, daytime heating aided in new thunderstorm development across southeast Arizona, which eventually produced a strong outflow traveling northward into Pinal County. The strong outflow boundary generated isolated dense blowing dust in Pinal County.
episodes.172479: A line of severe thunderstorms tracked across portions of eastern Iowa during the evening hours of July 23rd  and into northwest Illinois during the early morning of Sunday July 24th. Storms produced mainly damaging winds along their path, with numerous reports of structure, tree, and power line damage from Buchanan County Iowa east into Jo Daviess County Illinois. The Dubuque County Airport measured a 67 MPH wind gust as storms passed.
episodes.172484: A line of severe thunderstorms tracked from eastern Iowa into northwest Illinois during the early morning of Sunday July 24, 2022. Storms produced mainly damaging winds along their path, with numerous reports of structure, tree, and power line damage from  into Jo Daviess County Illinois.
episodes.172498: A combination of weak steering flow and tropical moisture resulted in slow moving thunderstorms with torrential downpours that produced flash flooding in Albany.  In addition, a few severe storms occurred with damaging winds.
episodes.172561: A late evening thunderstorm developed over Knox County, and produced wind gusts that blew down trees.
episodes.172612: A mid-level area of high shifted east and decreased in amplitude which opened the door for increased moisture, a classical medium to high end monsoonal pattern.
episodes.172613: A mid-level area of high shifted east and decreased in amplitude which opened the door for increased moisture, a classical medium to high end monsoonal pattern.
episodes.172685: Scattered thunderstorms moved west across southeast Arizona during the late night hours of July 23 into the morning of July 24. One storm produced a severe wind gust near Sierra Vista.
episodes.172686: Scattered thunderstorms moved northwest across southeast Arizona during the afternoon and evening. Storms produced heavy rain and flash flooding in Clifton, on the Tohono O'odham Nation and in western Pima County. Isolated flash flooding, wind damage and blowing dust occurred in other locations.
episodes.172773: Some drier low level air started moving into southern New Mexico, but modest mid level moisture remained across the area. Gusty winds and flash flooding were reported with the stronger storms that developed in Grant and Otero counties.
episodes.172778: Two rounds of storms moved across western Wisconsin on July 23rd. The first occurred in the afternoon and produced a tornado and wind damage. A brief EF0 tornado occurred just east of La Crosse (La Crosse County) that damaged trees along its path. The storms also produced high winds that caused considerable damage in and near Stoddard (Vernon County). A camper was blown over injuring the occupants and numerous trees and power lines were blown down. Trees were also blown down from near Viroqua (Vernon County) east to Ontario (Vernon County) and La Farge (Vernon County). The second round of storms occurred in the late evening and blew down trees near Wauzeka (Crawford County).
episodes.172782: A line of storms moved across northeast Iowa during the evening of July 23rd. These storms produced an EF1 tornado west of Waukon (Allamakee County) that damaged a farm and trees. Strong thunderstorm winds caused extensive damage to several buildings at the community college in Calmar (Winneshiek County) and flipped over a couple vehicles. The public school athletic fields in Calmar were also heavily damaged. The press box was blown off the high school football stands, metal light poles were downed at the softball field, and metal bleachers were thrown over a fence and onto the field. In Waukon, the roofs were damaged on numerous buildings and several trees and power lines were blown down. The Governor of Iowa issued a disaster proclamation for Allamakee, Clayton and Winneshiek Counties.
episodes.172795: Weak steering currents allowed thunderstorms to move slowly and produce localized heavy rainfall.
episodes.172946: Scattered thunderstorms developed over western North Carolina, mainly during the evening. A few of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts.
episodes.172953: Scattered thunderstorms developed across upstate South Carolina during the afternoon. One of the storms produced a microburst that caused significant damage in Union County.
